text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs that can understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns they learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites and articles. Users communicate with an LLM through prompts, and writing clear, specific prompts, known as prompt engineering, helps get better answers. LLMs can write texts, translate languages, summarise information and answer questions quickly. However, they also have limits. They sometimes give wrong information, cannot truly understand meaning, and may repeat biases found in their training data. For these reasons, their answers should always be checked.
